In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TME surgery should be performed to the distal rectum in both middle and distally located rectal cancer.
the distal mesoretum should be dissected in both distal and middle rectal cancer.
the distribution and metastasis of LNs in mesorectum is more complicated than we have thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mesorectal lymphatics are a complex network that is not only distributed in the mesorectal fat but also in the mesorectoral fascia and the rectal wall.
the distribution and metastasis pattern of LNs within the mesorectal fat were not consistent with the spread of the primary cancer, but the metastatic rate of mLNs was associated with the T stage.
the mLN metastasis pattern was not consistent with the primary tumour location, but the mLN metastatic incidence was higher in the distally located tumours.
The main takeaway from our work is that
small LNs are important in the staging of rectal cancer.
the distribution of LNs in the mesorectal area is not random and that the distribution of mLN is not related to tumour location.
small LNs should be included in the LN evaluation, and that the distribution of mLNs is not uniform in the mesorectal area.
